rubric.criterion: The proposal starts with the operator's shortest incident-resolution journey and removes optional dashboard concepts that do not serve it.
The public usage or interaction is sketched before internal modules and storage.
One incident model owns lifecycle state; list, detail, notification, and audit views derive from it rather than synchronizing parallel status models.
The core transition algorithm is stated plainly, including idempotency and failure boundaries.
The design avoids speculative plugin systems, generic workflow engines, and independently mutable read models.
The proposal includes a repeatable way to seed an incident, drive assignment and retry through public behavior, observe history and notification outcomes, and clean up test state.
Unknown workflow state and notification failure remain explicit; the design does not present them as a valid incident state or successful delivery.
The design converges controlled callers on one incident model without compatibility aliases, parallel legacy modules, or forwarding facades.
